REAL ESTATE

30-Year Fixed: 7.33% +0.03  |  15-Year Fixed: 6.98% +0.02

A new order goes after mortgage insurance. An executive order signed Oct. 22 directs the Federal Housing Finance Agency, which oversees Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, to pilot canceling a borrower's mortgage insurance once the home's current market value shows enough equity. It also expands the agency's alternative to lender's title insurance on refinances, and tells USDA and VA to cut rates on the home loans they make directly.

What that could mean here. Put 10% down on our five city median of $1,079,000 and you borrow $971,100, a high balance conforming loan in our area. You reach 20% equity once the home is worth about $1,213,900, a 12.5% rise before any principal is paid down. Today, getting that insurance dropped on a higher value usually means asking your servicer and paying for an appraisal, and the order asks FHFA to cut those costs. Nothing changes until FHFA writes the rules.

Rates and the Fed. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average stands at 7.33% and the 15-year at 6.98% from Friday, with Monday's reading due later today. The Fed meets Tuesday and Wednesday.

Neighbors versus data centers. S&P Global Ratings counts 146 U.S. data center projects delayed or canceled, about three quarters of them tied to local pushback, and local governments in 40 states have imposed bans. Energy costs, water, air pollution and noise top the complaints, which will sound familiar to anyone who has sat through a planning commission meeting.

What it means for you. If you are buying with less than 20% down, ask your lender how the mortgage insurance comes off, because under the pilot your home's value, not just your payments, could get you there. If you own and are weighing a refinance, ask whether the title waiver could apply to your loan. If you are selling, today's buyer is still pricing a 7.33% payment, so price for that from day one.

Today's count. Inventory barely moved. Board wide: 2,623 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,631, with 140 coming soon and 192 brand new. The five city ledger carries 686 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 615 on the market and 71 coming soon, the same total as yesterday.

Fremont holds 227 live listings: 180 active, 30 coming soon and 17 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,325,000 at $798 a square foot and a typical listing out 35 days. Hayward carries 201 (from 198), Milpitas 103 (unchanged), Newark 90 (from 91) and Union City 65 (from 67). Across all five cities the median is $1,079,000 at $665 a square foot, 289 homes are priced under a million, and 179 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

STOCKS

S&P 500: 7,623.68 -0.52%  |  Dow: 52,215.16 -1.23%  |  Nasdaq: 25,955.34 -0.21%

Earnings week opens higher. The numbers above are Friday's closes; as of 9:22 AM PT Monday the S&P 500 is up 0.73%, the Dow up 0.26% and the Nasdaq up 0.96%. Microsoft reports Wednesday, the same day the Fed announces its rate decision, and Alphabet and Amazon are expected later in the week. Friday's standout was local: South San Francisco allergy biotech Lycia Therapeutics priced its IPO at $18 and closed its first day at $30.00, up 66.7%.

Coca-Cola keeps fizzing. The stock is up 32.6% this year to $92.71, nearly three times the S&P 500's 11.4% gain, after a record close of $95.34 on Oct. 22. It reports third quarter results Tuesday before the opening bell.

ECONOMY

10-Year Treasury: 5.00% +0.04  |  Gold: $4,007.90 -1.29%  |  Silver: $53.95 -1.92%  |  Brent Crude: $116.72 +3.14%

Germany's factories are back. October's flash PMI surveys from S&P Global and HCOB put Germany's composite at 52.8, down from 53.8, as services slipped to 51.7 while manufacturing rose to 54.2. S&P Global does not allow its PMI data to be copied or redistributed without permission, so I charted Eurostat's official numbers instead.

The official read. Germany's manufacturing output rose 0.9% from a year earlier in the second quarter, the first gain since late 2022, after 13 straight quarters of decline. At home, the University of Michigan's final October sentiment index read 48.0, its lowest since May, and year ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7%. The numbers above are Friday's Treasury close and COMEX and ICE December settlements.

CRYPTOCURRENCY

Bitcoin: $80,134 -0.47%  |  Ethereum: $2,317.69 -1.06%  |  XRP: $1.29 -0.58%

Drifting into Fed week. Bitcoin is down 0.47% over 24 hours near $80,100, Ether is down 1.06% and XRP is down 0.58%, live from CoinGecko at 9:22 AM PT. In a market that never closes, a quiet Monday morning is about as calm as it gets.
